# Goal: Analyze GC-ECD and GC-IRMS data for N~2~O reduction to N~2~ by purified *Pseudomonas stutzeri* (aka *Stutzerimonas stutzeri*) nitrous oxide reductase (N2OR).

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

#Load packages.
```{r load_packages}
library(ggplot2) #For making pretty graphs
library(tidyverse) #For data tidying (changing dataframe organization, etc)
library(modelr) #provides rmse() function
library(egg) #provides a way to save ggplots with specified sizes
library(plotrix) #allows for standard error of the mean calculations
library(here) #Used to create file paths relative to top-level directory.
library(outliers) #used for Grubbs' test for outliers
library(nlstools) #provides preview function and other functions for nls models
```

#Naming conventions

Bulk N ($\delta$^15^N^bulk^) is abbreviated as delta_N.


$\delta$^18^O^N~2~O = delta_18O

"Fractionation factor" (normally abbreviated as $\alpha$) is abbreviated as `ff` to avoid confusion with N^$\alpha$^.

Other Greek letters are spelled out in object names. For example:

Enrichment factor ($\epsilon$) = `epsilon`

Other abbreviations

- lm    linear regression model

- KIE   kinetic isotope effect

- sd    standard deviation

- se    standard error

- SP    site preference

#Import ECD_samples: GC-ECD input table

- Samples collected 9/29/2025 and 10/14/2025 (69 samples total)
  - N2OR_2 timepoints 40, 45, and 60 min removed - more N2O was accidentally added to rxn bottle 2 before the 40 min timepoint
- Use this table as the input table for all subsequent analysis with GC-ECD data.
- Use the data in this table to plot Figure 2.
```{r import_ECD_samples}
ECD_samples <- read.table(here("data/input/ECD_samples.csv"),sep = ",", header = TRUE )
```

#Make initial_N2O table with average initial N2O +/- sd for each replicate and overall average for all 6 replicates
```{r initial_N2O}
#Make table with initial N_s0 and sd_N_s0 for each replicate.
initial_N2O <- tibble(
  Replicate = vector(length = 7, mode = "expression"),
  Data = vector(length = 7, mode = "expression"),
  Time_min = vector(length = 7, mode = "numeric"),
  N_s0 = vector(length = 7, mode = "numeric"),
  sd_N_s0 = vector(length = 7, mode = "numeric")
)

#Fill table
initial_N2O <- initial_N2O %>% mutate(
  Replicate = c(
    "N2OR_1", "N2OR_2", "N2OR_3","no_enzyme_1", "no_enzyme_2", "no_enzyme_3", "All"
  ),
  
  Data = c(
    rep("average of 2 initial measurements", 6),
    "average of all 6 initial measurements"
  ),
  
  Time_min = 0
)

#For each replicate, calculate initial N2O (N_s0).
##N_s0 is the average of the 0 timepoints.

##N2OR_1
initial_N2O$N_s0[(which(initial_N2O$Replicate == "N2OR_1"))] = 
  mean(
  unlist(select(
    filter(ECD_samples, Replicate == "N2OR_1" & Total_time_min < 0), Total_N2O_umole)
)
)

##N2OR_2
initial_N2O$N_s0[(which(initial_N2O$Replicate == "N2OR_2"))] = 
  mean(
  unlist(select(
    filter(ECD_samples, Replicate == "N2OR_2" & Total_time_min < 0), Total_N2O_umole)
)
)

##N2OR_3
initial_N2O$N_s0[(which(initial_N2O$Replicate == "N2OR_3"))] = 
  mean(

)

initial_N2O$N_s0[(which(initial_N2O$Replicate == "no_enzyme_1"))] =
```

#Figure 2. Plot Total N2O umol (excluding spiked samples) vs Time_min (initial timepoints  = 0 min) for ppt; plot initial average N2O for each replicate (N_s0)
```{r plot_total_N2O_v_time_min_N_s0}
ECD_reorg <- rbind(
  filter(ECD_samples, Replicate == "N2OR_1"),
  filter(ECD_samples, Replicate == "N2OR_2"),
  filter(ECD_samples, Replicate == "N2OR_3"),
  filter(ECD_samples, Replicate == "no_enzyme_1"),
  filter(ECD_samples, Replicate == "no_enzyme_2"),
  filter(ECD_samples, Replicate == "no_enzyme_3")
)
  
#Add new column to table that combines N_s0 at time = 0 with Total_N2O_umol at all other timepoints

##N_s0 is the average of the 0 timepoints measured for an individual replicate.

ECD_reorg_2 <- ECD_reorg %>% mutate(
  y_N2O = 0
)

n = length(ECD_reorg_2$y_N2O)

for (i in 1:n) {
  if(ECD_reorg_2$Time_min[i] == 0) {
    ECD_reorg_2$y_N2O[i] = ECD_reorg_2$N_s0[i]
  }
    else if(ECD_reorg_2$Time_min[i] >0) {
    ECD_reorg_2$y_N2O[i] = ECD_reorg_2$Total_N2O_umole[i]
    }
}

(plot_total_N2O_v_time_N_s0 <- 
  ggplot()+
   geom_point(data = ECD_reorg_2, mapping = 
         aes(x = Time_min, y = y_N2O, shape = Replicate, color = Replicate), size = 2)+
    
   
   geom_vline(data = ECD_reorg, mapping = aes(xintercept = 0))+
   
    scale_color_manual(name = "Replicate",
    values = c("#000000", "#B94685", "#56B4E9","#1E5C19", "#D55E00", "#999999"),
    labels = c(
    expression(paste(bold(N[2]), bold("OR 1"))),
    expression(paste(bold(N[2]), bold("OR 2"))),
    expression(paste(bold(N[2]), bold("OR 3"))),    
    expression(paste(bold("No Enzyme 1"))),
    expression(paste(bold("No Enzyme 2"))),
    expression(paste(bold("No Enzyme 3")))  
  ))+
 
  scale_shape_manual(name = "Replicate",
    values = c(16, 16, 16, 8, 8, 8),
    labels = c(
    expression(paste(bold(N[2]), bold("OR 1"))),
    expression(paste(bold(N[2]), bold("OR 2"))),
    expression(paste(bold(N[2]), bold("OR 3"))),    
    expression(paste(bold("No Enzyme 1"))),
    expression(paste(bold("No Enzyme 2"))),
    expression(paste(bold("No Enzyme 3")))  
  ))+  
  
  #Make graph pretty
  theme_bw()+
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank())+
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())+
    
  #format axis titles
  theme(axis.title = element_text(size = 16))+
```

#Fit models to ECD data for N2OR1-3 using Total_N2O_umole as the dependent variable (y = A = Total_N2O_umole).

- Use the rate constant (k) determined for each replicate to calculate Total_N2O_umole and f for IRMS data.

##Exponential decay formula
A = A_0*e^(-kt)
where

- A = N2O umol = Total_N2O_umole = N2O in rxn bottle + N2O removed during previous sampling for ECD
- A_0 = initial N2O umol = N_s0
- k = rate constant
- t = time (min)

##Note: I get an error when I try to use N_s0 as a parameter name.
```{r exp_decay_model}
#Define exponential decay formula
exp_decay <- as.formula(Total_N2O_umole ~A_0*exp(-k*Time_min))

#N2OR_1
##preview model fit to test the starting values of the model parameters (A_0, k) 
preview(exp_decay, data = filter(ECD_samples, Replicate == "N2OR_1"),
                                 start = list(A_0 = 4, k = 0.04), variable = 6)

##fit and name exponential decay model for N2OR_1
exp_decay_N2OR_1 <- nls(exp_decay, data = filter(ECD_samples, Replicate == "N2OR_1"), start = list(A_0 = 4, k = 0.04))

summary(exp_decay_N2OR_1)
(rmse(exp_decay_N2OR_1, data = filter(ECD_samples, Replicate == "N2OR_1")))

#N2OR_2
##preview model fit to test the starting values of the model parameters (A_0, k) 
preview(exp_decay, data = filter(ECD_samples, Replicate == "N2OR_2"),
                                 start = list(A_0 = 4, k = 0.04), variable = 6)

##fit and name exponential decay model for N2OR_2
exp_decay_N2OR_2 <- nls(exp_decay, data = filter(ECD_samples, Replicate == "N2OR_2"), start = list(A_0 = 4, k = 0.04))

summary(exp_decay_N2OR_2)
(rmse(exp_decay_N2OR_2, data = filter(ECD_samples, Replicate == "N2OR_2")))

#N2OR_3
##preview model fit to test the starting values of the model parameters (A_0, k) 
preview(exp_decay, data = filter(ECD_samples, Replicate == "N2OR_3"),
                                 start = list(A_0 = 4, k = 0.04), variable = 6)

##fit and name exponential decay model for N2OR_3
exp_decay_N2OR_3 <- nls(exp_decay, data = filter(ECD_samples, Replicate == "N2OR_3"), start = list(A_0 = 4, k = 0.04))

summary(exp_decay_N2OR_3)
(rmse(exp_decay_N2OR_3, data = filter(ECD_samples, Replicate == "N2OR_3")))
```
Preview graph: actual values  - black circles; predicted values - red +
The dependent variable (Total_N2O_umole) is plotted on the y-axis.
An independent variable (of our choosing) is plotted on the x-axis. In this case, the independent variable is time. (Set by the 'variable = 6' argument in the preview function; Time_min is the 6th column in the dataset.)

Parameters A_0 and k are pretty close to Excel's estimates for all three replicates

#Make table with predicted total N2O values (predicted using exponential decay models) for N2OR1-3
```{r ECD_samples_pred}
ECD_samples_pred <- select(
  filter(ECD_samples, Replicate == "N2OR_1" | Replicate == "N2OR_2" | Replicate == "N2OR_3"), 
  Sample_name, Replicate, Time_min, Total_N2O_umole, N_s0) %>%
  
  mutate(
    Total_N2O_umole_pred = c(
      predict(exp_decay_N2OR_1),
      predict(exp_decay_N2OR_2),
      predict(exp_decay_N2OR_3)
    )
  )

(ECD_samples_pred)
```

#Import IRMS data

The same reaction bottles with purified N2OR were sampled for GC-ECD and for GC-IRMS. GC-ECD concentration measurements were plotted vs time and used to back-calculate N~2~O concentrations in IRMS samples.

- 9/29/2025 Experiments
  - Controls
    - no_enzyme_1 (12 samples; 0-60 min)
    - no_enzyme_2 (11 samples; 0-45 min)
  - Rxns with enzyme
    - N2OR_1 (11 samples; 0-45 min)
    - N2OR_2 (9 samples; 0-35 min)
  
- 10/14/2025 Experiments
  - Controls
    - no_enzyme_3 (12 samples; 0-60 min)
  -Rxn with enzyme
    - N2OR_3 (12 samples, 0-60 min)

- 67 samples total
```{r import_IRMS_data}
IRMS_all <- read.table(here("data/input/IRMS_input_2025-11-25.csv"),sep = ",", header = TRUE )
```

#IRMS: Remove unneeded data and add N_s0 (calculated from ECD data)

- Rows where detector was saturated (no isotopic data was collected)
  - Sample_name: rep 3 02
  - Sample_name: rep 3 60 min
  
- N_s0 = average of the two time = 0 Total_N2O_umole measurements from the ECD data

```{r IRMS}
IRMS <- IRMS_all %>%
  #Remove samples where detector was saturated
  filter(
    Sample_name != "rep 3 02" &
    Sample_name != "rep 3 60 min"
) %>%
  
  #Change class of delta_N to numeric. (For some reason, the class was set to "character" when the data was imported.)
  mutate(
    delta_N = as.numeric(delta_N)
  )
  
#Add N_s0 to table (average of Total_N2O_umole from initial ECD measurements)
##Add empty column for N_s0
IRMS$N_s0 = 0

##no_enzyme_1
IRMS$N_s0[(which(IRMS$Replicate == "no_enzyme_1"))] = 
  mean(
  unlist(select(
    filter(ECD_samples, Replicate == "no_enzyme_1" & Total_time_min < 0), Total_N2O_umole)
)
)

##no_enzyme_2
IRMS$N_s0[(which(IRMS$Replicate == "no_enzyme_2"))] = 
  mean(
  unlist(select(
    filter(ECD_samples, Replicate == "no_enzyme_2" & Total_time_min < 0), Total_N2O_umole)
)
)

##no_enzyme_3
IRMS$N_s0[(which(IRMS$Replicate == "no_enzyme_3"))] = 
  mean(
  unlist(select(
    filter(ECD_samples, Replicate == "no_enzyme_3" & Total_time_min < 0), Total_N2O_umole)
)
)

##N2OR_1
IRMS$N_s0[(which(IRMS$Replicate == "N2OR_1"))] = 
  mean(
  unlist(select(
    filter(ECD_samples, Replicate == "N2OR_1" & Total_time_min < 0), Total_N2O_umole)
)
)

##N2OR_2
IRMS$N_s0[(which(IRMS$Replicate == "N2OR_2"))] = 
  mean(
  unlist(select(
    filter(ECD_samples, Replicate == "N2OR_2" & Total_time_min < 0), Total_N2O_umole)
)
)

##N2OR_3
IRMS$N_s0[(which(IRMS$Replicate == "N2OR_3"))] = 
  mean(
  unlist(select(
    filter(ECD_samples, Replicate == "N2OR_3" & Total_time_min < 0), Total_N2O_umole)
```

#IRMS: Convert delta values to R values and add the R values to the table.

R_std values for Elementar IRMS taken from Skrzypek, G. and Dunn, P. J. H.: Absolute isotope ratios defining isotope scales used in isotope ratio mass spectrometers and optical isotope instruments, Rapid Commun. Mass. Sp., 34, e8890,
https://doi.org/10.1002/rcm.8890, 2020.

```{r IRMS_add_R}
IRMS <- IRMS %>% mutate(
 R_std_N = 0.0036765, #R (15N/14N) for atmospheric N2
 R_N = (delta_N/1000 + 1)*R_std_N,
 R_alpha = (delta_alpha/1000 + 1)*R_std_N,
 R_beta = (delta_beta/1000 + 1)*R_std_N,
 R_SP = (SP/1000 + 1)*R_std_N,
 
 R_std_18O = 0.00200520, #R (18O/16O) for VSMOW
 R_18O = (delta_18O/1000 + 1)*R_std_18O
)
```

#Calculate delta_s0_meas (average of measured initial delta values) for delta_N, delta_alpha, delta_beta, and delta_18O. Use time 0 measurements for both controls and reactions with N2OR.

- The measured delta_so values from Table 2 were calculated here.
```{r delta_s0_meas_all_data}
#n = number of delta types; in this case, n = 5
n <- 5

#m = number of models; in this case, m = 1 because we're only using one model/method to calculate delta_s0_meas

m <- 1


#Make blank table with mean and standard error for initial delta values
initial_deltas <- tibble(
    Model = vector(length = n*m, mode = "expression"),
    Data = vector(length = n*m, mode = "expression"),
    Replicate = vector(length = n*m, mode = "expression"),
    Delta_type = vector(length = n*m, mode = "expression"),

    delta_s0_meas = vector(length = n*m, mode = "numeric"),
    se_delta_s0_meas = vector(length = n*m, mode = "numeric")
)

#Add info to table
initial_deltas <- initial_deltas %>% mutate(
  Model = "Average all time = 0 measurements",
  Data = c(
    "N2OR Replicates 1-3 and No Enzyme Controls 1-3"
),

  Replicate = "all data pooled",

  Delta_type = c(
    "delta_N",
    "delta_alpha",
    "delta_beta",
    "SP",
    "delta_18O"
  )
)


#Use time 0 measurements for no_enzyme_control 1-3 and N2OR1-3
#Mean delta_s0 value for delta_N (bulk)
initial_deltas$delta_s0_meas[1] = 
  mean(
  unlist(select(
    filter(IRMS, Time_min == 0), delta_N)
)
)

#Mean delta_s0 value for delta_alpha
initial_deltas$delta_s0_meas[2] = 
  mean(
  unlist(select(
    filter(IRMS, Time_min == 0), delta_alpha)
)
)
  
#Mean delta_s0 value for delta_beta
initial_deltas$delta_s0_meas[3] =
  mean(
  unlist(select(
    filter(IRMS, Time_min == 0), delta_beta)
)
)
  
#Mean delta_s0 value for SP
initial_deltas$delta_s0_meas[4] =
  mean(
  unlist(select(
    filter(IRMS, Time_min == 0), SP)
)
)
  
#Mean delta_s0 value for delta_18O
initial_deltas$delta_s0_meas[5] =
  mean(
  unlist(select(
    filter(IRMS, Time_min == 0), delta_18O)
)
)

#Standard error calcs: Use time 0 measurements for no_enzyme_control 1-3 and N2OR1-3
#Standard error for delta_s0 value for delta_N (bulk)
initial_deltas$se_delta_s0_meas[1] = 
  std.error(
  unlist(select(
    filter(IRMS, Time_min == 0), delta_N)
)
)

#std.error delta_s0 value for delta_alpha
initial_deltas$se_delta_s0_meas[2] = 
  std.error(
  unlist(select(
    filter(IRMS, Time_min == 0), delta_alpha)
)
)
  
#std.error delta_s0 value for delta_beta
initial_deltas$se_delta_s0_meas[3] =
  std.error(
  unlist(select(
    filter(IRMS, Time_min == 0), delta_beta)
)
)
  
#std.error delta_s0 value for SP
initial_deltas$se_delta_s0_meas[4] =
  std.error(
  unlist(select(
    filter(IRMS, Time_min == 0), SP)
)
)
  
#std.error delta_s0 value for delta_18O
initial_deltas$se_delta_s0_meas[5] =
  std.error(
  unlist(select(
    filter(IRMS, Time_min == 0), delta_18O)
)
)

(initial_deltas)
```

#IRMS: Add initial delta values to table and calculate corresponding initial R values.

- Initial deltas were calculated by averaging the initial delta values from all 6 replicates (3 controls + 3 w/ enzyme).
```{r IRMS_add_initial_deltas}
IRMS <- IRMS %>%
  mutate(
    delta_N_0 =
      initial_deltas$delta_s0_meas[which(initial_deltas$Delta_type == "delta_N")],
    
    delta_alpha_0 = 
      initial_deltas$delta_s0_meas[which(initial_deltas$Delta_type == "delta_alpha")],
    
    delta_beta_0 = 
    initial_deltas$delta_s0_meas[which(initial_deltas$Delta_type == "delta_beta")],
    
    SP_0 = initial_deltas$delta_s0_meas[which(initial_deltas$Delta_type == "SP")],
    
    delta_18O_0 = initial_deltas$delta_s0_meas[which(initial_deltas$Delta_type == "delta_18O")],
    
    #Convert delta values to R values
    R_N_0 = (delta_N_0/1000 + 1)*R_std_N,
    R_alpha_0 = (delta_alpha_0/1000 + 1)*R_std_N,
    R_beta_0 = (delta_beta_0/1000 + 1)*R_std_N,
    R_SP_0 = (SP_0/1000 + 1)*R_std_N,
    R_18O_0 = (delta_18O_0/1000 + 1)*R_std_18O
  )
```


#IRMS_N2OR_rxns: Calculate N2O umol, f, etc
##Use these f values for all subsequent (Rayleigh) calculations

Total_N2O_umole = A = N_s0*e^(-kt)
  - N_s0 = initial N2O = average of Total_N2O_umole for the two ECD measurements taken at time = 0
  - k = rate constant from exponential decay model
  - t = Time_min
  
##Note: In theory, we could also use A_0 as the initial N2O value.
  - A_0 = coefficient from exponential decay model = summary(exp_decay_N2OR_1)$coefficients[1,1]
  - However, the exponential decay model slightly underestimates initial N2O (A_0 < N_s0). This leads to f values that are slightly lower than they should be.
  - For example, at time = 0, f should equal 1: f = N_s0/N_s0. But if we use A_0,
  f is defined as A_0/N_s0, causing f to be less than 1 (i.e., f = 0.97). This is misleading because it makes it look like the time 0 IRMS measurements were actually taken after the reaction was started.
```{r IRMS_N2OR_rxns}
IRMS_N2OR_rxns <- IRMS %>% filter(
  Replicate == "N2OR_1" | Replicate == "N2OR_2" | Replicate == "N2OR_3"
) %>%
  mutate(
    #Add empty columns for A_0 and k (coefficients from exponential decay model)
    A_0 = 0,
    k = 0
  )

#Add A_0 and k determined from exponential decay model fitted to ECD data
##N2OR_1
IRMS_N2OR_rxns$A_0[which(IRMS_N2OR_rxns$Replicate == "N2OR_1")] = summary(exp_decay_N2OR_1)$coefficients[1,1]

IRMS_N2OR_rxns$k[which(IRMS_N2OR_rxns$Replicate == "N2OR_1")] = summary(exp_decay_N2OR_1)$coefficients[2,1]

##N2OR_2
IRMS_N2OR_rxns$A_0[which(IRMS_N2OR_rxns$Replicate == "N2OR_2")] = summary(exp_decay_N2OR_2)$coefficients[1,1]

IRMS_N2OR_rxns$k[which(IRMS_N2OR_rxns$Replicate == "N2OR_2")] = summary(exp_decay_N2OR_2)$coefficients[2,1]

##N2OR_3:
IRMS_N2OR_rxns$A_0[which(IRMS_N2OR_rxns$Replicate == "N2OR_3")] = summary(exp_decay_N2OR_3)$coefficients[1,1]

IRMS_N2OR_rxns$k[which(IRMS_N2OR_rxns$Replicate == "N2OR_3")] = summary(exp_decay_N2OR_3)$coefficients[2,1]

#Add Total_N2O_umole calculated using A_0 and k coefficients from exponential decay model (fitted to ECD data)

IRMS_N2OR_rxns <- IRMS_N2OR_rxns %>% mutate(
  Total_N2O_umole = N_s0*exp(-k*Time_min),
  
  #Calculate f where N_s = Total_N2O_umole (calc'd from exp. decay model) and N_s0 = average of the two 0 timepoints from the ECD data
  f = Total_N2O_umole/N_s0,
  one_minus_f = 1-f,
  lnf = log(f)  
)

#Write table to csv
##One of the SI tables will be a subset of this table.
write.csv(IRMS_N2OR_rxns, here("data/output/IRMS_N2OR_rxns.csv"), row.names = TRUE)
```

#Make blank table (tibble) for storing values extracted from each model.
```{r summary_blank}
#n = number of loops; in this case, the number of replicates
n = 1

#m = number of models; in this case, m = 1 because we're only using one model for each table

m <- 1

blank_tb <- function(n, m = 1) {
  tibble(
    Model = vector(length = n*m, mode = "expression"),
    Data = vector(length = n*m, mode = "expression"),
    Replicate = vector(length = n*m, mode = "expression"),
    Delta_type = vector(length = n*m, mode = "expression"),
  
    Multiple_R_squared = vector(length = n*m, mode = "numeric"),
    RMSE_lm = vector(length = n*m, mode = "numeric"), #RMSE value for delta_p prediction from linear Rayleigh model
  
    f_min = vector(length = n*m, mode = "numeric"),
    f_max = vector(length = n*m, mode = "numeric"),
  
    delta_s0_meas = vector(length = n*m, mode = "numeric"),
    se_delta_s0_meas = vector(length = n*m, mode = "numeric"),
    
    delta_s0_calc = vector(length = n*m, mode = "numeric"),
    se_delta_s0_calc = vector(length = n*m, mode = "numeric"),
    
    epsilon = vector(length = n*m, mode = "numeric"),
    se_epsilon = vector(length = n*m, mode = "numeric"),
    
    ff = vector(length = n*m, mode = "numeric"),
    se_ff = vector(length = n*m, mode = "numeric"),
    
    KIE = vector(length = n*m, mode = "numeric"),
    se_KIE = vector(length = n*m, mode = "numeric"),
    
    pval_epsilon = vector(length = n*m, mode = "numeric")
)
}
```

#Make table with values extracted from the Rayleigh model (x=lnf, y = delta) for delta_N, delta_alpha, delta_beta, SP, and delta_18O (N2OR1-3 combined; all data)

  - Make a separate row in the table for each delta type (delta_N, delta_alpha, delta_beta, SP, and delta_18O)
```{r N2OR_ray_table, warning=FALSE}
#n = number of loops; in this case, the number of rows in the table
n <- 5

#m = number of models; in this case, m = 1 because we're only using one model (standard Rayleigh)

m <- 1

#Make empty table to store results
N2OR_ray <- blank_tb(n, m)

N2OR_ray <- mutate(N2OR_ray,
  Model = c(
    "Rayleigh (x = ln(f))"
  ),
  
  Data = c(
    "N2OR Replicates 1-3"
),

  Replicate = "pooled N2OR_1-3",

  Delta_type = c(
    "delta_N",
    "delta_alpha",
    "delta_beta",
    "SP",
    "delta_18O"
  )
) 

for (i in 1:n) {
    data <- IRMS_N2OR_rxns
    
  
  if(i == 1){ #First row: delta_N
    y <- IRMS_N2OR_rxns$delta_N
    x <- IRMS_N2OR_rxns$lnf
  } else if(i == 2){ #Second row: delta_alpha
    y <- IRMS_N2OR_rxns$delta_alpha
    x <- IRMS_N2OR_rxns$lnf
  } else if(i == 3){ #Third row: delta_beta
    y <- IRMS_N2OR_rxns$delta_beta
    x <- IRMS_N2OR_rxns$lnf    
  } else if(i == 4){ #Fourth row: SP
    y <- IRMS_N2OR_rxns$SP
    x <- IRMS_N2OR_rxns$lnf        
  } else if (i == 5){ #Fifth row: delta_18O
    y <- IRMS_N2OR_rxns$delta_18O
    x <- IRMS_N2OR_rxns$lnf    
  }
  

  
  #Apply standard Rayleigh model where x = lnf and y = delta_N, delta_alpha, or delta_beta, SP, or delta_18O
    lm_delta <- lm(y ~ x, data = data)
    
    #Fill in table w/ values extracted from standard Rayleigh model
    N2OR_ray$Multiple_R_squared[i] = summary(lm_delta)$r.squared
    N2OR_ray$RMSE_lm[i] = rmse(model = lm_delta, data = data)
  
    N2OR_ray$f_min[i] = min(data$f)
    N2OR_ray$f_max[i] = max(data$f)
    
    N2OR_ray$delta_s0_meas[i] = initial_deltas$delta_s0_meas[i]
    N2OR_ray$se_delta_s0_meas[i] = initial_deltas$se_delta_s0_meas[i]
  
    N2OR_ray$delta_s0_calc[i] = summary(lm_delta)$coefficients[1,1]
    N2OR_ray$se_delta_s0_calc[i] = summary(lm_delta)$coefficients[1,2]
    
    N2OR_ray$epsilon[i] = as.numeric( lm_delta$coefficients[2])
    N2OR_ray$se_epsilon[i] = summary( lm_delta)$coefficients[2,2]
    
    N2OR_ray$ff[i] = 1 +  lm_delta$coefficients[2]/1000
    N2OR_ray$se_ff[i] = N2OR_ray$se_epsilon[i]/1000    
    
    N2OR_ray$KIE[i] = 1/N2OR_ray$ff[i]
    N2OR_ray$se_KIE[i] = abs(-1/(N2OR_ray$ff[i])^2*N2OR_ray$se_ff[i])
    
    N2OR_ray$pval_epsilon[i] = summary(lm_delta)$coefficients[2,4]
}

write.csv(N2OR_ray, here("data/output/N2OR_ray.csv"), row.names = TRUE)

(N2OR_ray)
```

#Early data: Make table with values extracted from the Rayleigh model (x=lnf, y = delta) for delta_N, delta_alpha, delta_beta, SP, and delta_18O (N2OR1-3 combined; f >= 0.4)

  - Make a separate row in the table for each delta type (delta_N, delta_alpha, delta_beta, SP, and delta_18O)
```{r N2OR_ray_early_table, warning=FALSE}
#n = number of loops; in this case, the number of rows in the table
n <- 5

#m = number of models; in this case, m = 1 because we're only using one model (standard Rayleigh)

m <- 1

#Make empty table to store results
N2OR_ray_early <- blank_tb(n, m)

N2OR_ray_early <- mutate(N2OR_ray_early,
  Model = c(
    "Rayleigh (x = ln(f))"
  ),
  
  Data = c(
    "N2OR Replicates 1-3; f >= 0.4"
),

  Replicate = "pooled N2OR_1-3",

  Delta_type = c(
    "delta_N",
    "delta_alpha",
    "delta_beta",
    "SP",
    "delta_18O"
  )
) 

for (i in 1:n) {
    data <- filter(IRMS_N2OR_rxns, f >= 0.4)
    
  
  if(i == 1){ #First row: delta_N
    y <- data$delta_N
    x <- data$lnf
  } else if(i == 2){ #Second row: delta_alpha
    y <- data$delta_alpha
    x <- data$lnf
  } else if(i == 3){ #Third row: delta_beta
    y <- data$delta_beta
    x <- data$lnf    
  } else if(i == 4){ #Fourth row: SP
    y <- data$SP
    x <- data$lnf        
  } else if (i == 5){ #Fifth row: delta_18O
    y <- data$delta_18O
    x <- data$lnf    
  }
  

  
  #Apply standard Rayleigh model where x = lnf and y = delta_N, delta_alpha, delta_beta, SP, or delta_18O
    lm_delta <- lm(y ~ x, data = data)
    
    #Fill in table w/ values extracted from standard Rayleigh model
    N2OR_ray_early$Multiple_R_squared[i] = summary(lm_delta)$r.squared
    N2OR_ray_early$RMSE_lm[i] = rmse(model = lm_delta, data = data)
  
    N2OR_ray_early$f_min[i] = min(data$f)
    N2OR_ray_early$f_max[i] = max(data$f)
    
    N2OR_ray_early$delta_s0_meas[i] = initial_deltas$delta_s0_meas[i]
    N2OR_ray_early$se_delta_s0_meas[i] = initial_deltas$se_delta_s0_meas[i]
  
    N2OR_ray_early$delta_s0_calc[i] = summary(lm_delta)$coefficients[1,1]
    N2OR_ray_early$se_delta_s0_calc[i] = summary(lm_delta)$coefficients[1,2]
    
    N2OR_ray_early$epsilon[i] = as.numeric( lm_delta$coefficients[2])
    N2OR_ray_early$se_epsilon[i] = summary( lm_delta)$coefficients[2,2]
    
    N2OR_ray_early$ff[i] = 1 +  lm_delta$coefficients[2]/1000
    N2OR_ray_early$se_ff[i] = N2OR_ray_early$se_epsilon[i]/1000    
    
    N2OR_ray_early$KIE[i] = 1/N2OR_ray_early$ff[i]
    N2OR_ray_early$se_KIE[i] = abs(-1/(N2OR_ray_early$ff[i])^2*N2OR_ray_early$se_ff[i])
    
    N2OR_ray_early$pval_epsilon[i] = summary(lm_delta)$coefficients[2,4]
}

write.csv(N2OR_ray_early, here("data/output/N2OR_ray_early.csv"), row.names = TRUE)

(N2OR_ray_early)
```

#Bulk N: Name the linear regression model for the Rayleigh equation for substrate without approximation where y = ln(f*(1+R_s0)/(1+R_s)) and x = ln(R_s/R_s0) (N2OR1-3 combined)

Eq. 39 from Hayes, 2004 and Eq. V.17 from Bigeleisen and Wolfsburg, 1958:
ln(R_s/R_s0) = epsilon*ln(f*(1+R_s0)/(1+R_s))

  - slope = epsilon

  - intercept = 0
```{r N2OR_lm_BW_N}
N2OR_lm_BW_N <- lm(
  log(R_N/R_N_0) ~ log(f*(1+R_N_0)/(1+R_N)), data = IRMS_N2OR_rxns
)

summary(N2OR_lm_BW_N)

#Multiply the intercept and slope (epsilon) by 1000 to convert to per mil:
##intercept
summary(N2OR_lm_BW_N)$coefficients[1,1]*1000

##slope (epsilon)
summary(N2OR_lm_BW_N)$coefficients[2,1]*1000
```
The epsilon value for bulk N calculated using the Bigeleisen-Wolfsburg version of the Rayleigh equation (N2OR_lm_BW_N) is very similar to the epsilon value calculated using Mariotti's approximation of the Rayleigh equation (N2OR_lm_delta_N).

#N_alpha: Name the linear regression model for the Rayleigh equation for substrate without approximation where y = ln(f*(1+R_s0)/(1+R_s)) and x = ln(R_s/R_s0) (N2OR1-3 combined)

Eq. 39 from Hayes, 2004 and Eq. V.17 from Bigeleisen and Wolfsburg, 1958:
ln(R_s/R_s0) = epsilon*ln(f*(1+R_s0)/(1+R_s))
```{r N2OR_lm_BW_alpha}
N2OR_lm_BW_alpha <- lm(
  log(R_alpha/R_alpha_0) ~ log(f*(1+R_alpha_0)/(1+R_alpha)), data = IRMS_N2OR_rxns
)

summary(N2OR_lm_BW_alpha)

#Multiply the intercept and slope (epsilon) by 1000 to convert to per mil:
##intercept
summary(N2OR_lm_BW_alpha)$coefficients[1,1]*1000

##slope (epsilon)
summary(N2OR_lm_BW_alpha)$coefficients[2,1]*1000
```
#N_beta: Name the linear regression model for the Rayleigh equation for substrate without approximation where y = ln(f*(1+R_s0)/(1+R_s)) and x = ln(R_s/R_s0) (N2OR1-3 combined)

Eq. 39 from Hayes, 2004 and Eq. V.17 from Bigeleisen and Wolfsburg, 1958:
ln(R_s/R_s0) = epsilon*ln(f*(1+R_s0)/(1+R_s))
```{r N2OR_lm_BW_beta}
N2OR_lm_BW_beta <- lm(
  log(R_beta/R_beta_0) ~ log(f*(1+R_beta_0)/(1+R_beta)), data = IRMS_N2OR_rxns
)

summary(N2OR_lm_BW_beta)

#Multiply the intercept and slope (epsilon) by 1000 to convert to per mil:
##intercept
summary(N2OR_lm_BW_beta)$coefficients[1,1]*1000

##slope (epsilon)
summary(N2OR_lm_BW_beta)$coefficients[2,1]*1000
```
#delta_18O: Name the linear regression model for the Rayleigh equation for substrate without approximation where y = ln(f*(1+R_s0)/(1+R_s)) and x = ln(R_s/R_s0) (N2OR1-3 combined)

Eq. 39 from Hayes, 2004 and Eq. V.17 from Bigeleisen and Wolfsburg, 1958:
ln(R_s/R_s0) = epsilon*ln(f*(1+R_s0)/(1+R_s))
```{r N2OR_lm_BW_18O}
N2OR_lm_BW_18O <- lm(
  log(R_18O/R_18O_0) ~ log(f*(1+R_18O_0)/(1+R_18O)), data = IRMS_N2OR_rxns
)

summary(N2OR_lm_BW_18O)

#Multiply the intercept and slope (epsilon) by 1000 to convert to per mil:
##intercept
summary(N2OR_lm_BW_18O)$coefficients[1,1]*1000

##slope (epsilon)
summary(N2OR_lm_BW_18O)$coefficients[2,1]*1000
```
- The epsilon value for delta_18O changes the most when the Rayleigh model without approximation (BW) is used instead of Mariotti's approximation of the Rayleigh equation (where y = delta and x = lnf).
  - w/o approx: epsilon_18O  = -13.5 per mil
  - w/ approx: epsilon_18O = -14.2 per mil

This is not surprising, as epsilon and especially delta_s0 are the largest for 18O (compared to 15N). Mariotti's approximation of the Rayleigh equation assumes that delta_s0 and epsilon are both small compared to 1 (i.e, relatively close to 0 per mil).

#IRMS_N2OR_BW: Make table with BW model values for x and y

```{r IRMS_N2OR_BW}
  y_N = log(R_N/R_N_0),
  x_N = log(f*(1+R_N_0)/(1+R_N)),
  
  ##N_alpha
  y_alpha = log(R_alpha/R_alpha_0),
  x_alpha = log(f*(1+R_alpha_0)/(1+R_alpha)),
  
  ##N_beta
  y_beta = log(R_beta/R_beta_0),
  x_beta = log(f*(1+R_beta_0)/(1+R_beta)),
  
  ##SP
  y_SP = log(R_SP/R_SP_0),
  x_SP = log(f*(1+R_SP_0)/(1+R_SP)),
  
  ##delta_18O
  y_18O = log(R_18O/R_18O_0),
  x_18O = log(f*(1+R_18O_0)/(1+R_18O))
)
```

```{r plot_N_SP_BW_legend}
#Make tidy table
##n = number of delta types/R types (4 in this case: bulk, alpha, beta, and SP)

IRMS_N2OR_BW_tidy <- tibble(
  Sample_name = rep(IRMS_N2OR_BW$Sample_name, n),
  Replicate = rep(IRMS_N2OR_BW$Replicate, n),
  Delta_type = c(
    rep("bulk", times = length(IRMS_N2OR_BW$Sample_name)),
    rep("alpha", times = length(IRMS_N2OR_BW$Sample_name)),
    rep("beta", times = length(IRMS_N2OR_BW$Sample_name)),
    rep("SP", times = length(IRMS_N2OR_BW$Sample_name))    
  ),
  x = c(
    IRMS_N2OR_BW$x_N,
    IRMS_N2OR_BW$x_alpha,
    IRMS_N2OR_BW$x_beta,
    IRMS_N2OR_BW$x_SP    
  ),
  
  y = c(
    IRMS_N2OR_BW$y_N,
    IRMS_N2OR_BW$y_alpha,
    IRMS_N2OR_BW$y_beta,
    IRMS_N2OR_BW$y_SP
  )
)

#Factor Delta_type so that data doesn't get sorted alphabetically in legend

(plot_N_SP_BW_legend <- 
  ggplot(data = IRMS_N2OR_BW_tidy)+
   geom_point(mapping = 
         aes(x = x, y = y, shape = Delta_type, color = Delta_type), size = 2)+   
    geom_smooth(mapping = aes(x = x, y = y, color = Delta_type), method = lm, se = FALSE)+
   
   #geom_vline(data = IRMS_N2OR_tidy, mapping = aes(xintercept = 0))+
   
    scale_color_manual(name = "R type",
    values = c("#999999", "#a6cee3","#1E5C19", "#CC79A7"),
    labels = c(
    expression(paste(bold(R^15),bold(N^bulk), sep="")),    
    expression(paste(bold(R^15),bold(N^alpha), sep="")),
    expression(paste(bold(R^15),bold(N^beta), sep="")),
    expression(paste(bold(R^15),bold(N^SP), sep=""))    
  ))+
 
  scale_shape_manual(name = "R type",
    values = c(16, 15, 17, 8),
    labels = c(
    expression(paste(bold(R^15),bold(N^bulk), sep="")),    
    expression(paste(bold(R^15),bold(N^alpha), sep="")),
    expression(paste(bold(R^15),bold(N^beta), sep="")),
    expression(paste(bold(R^15),bold(N^SP), sep=""))     
  ))+  
  
  #Make graph pretty
  theme_bw()+
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank())+
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())+
    
  #Add range for x-axis
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-2.1, 0.0001), breaks = c(-0.5*0:4),
                     labels = paste0(c(-0.5*0:4),""))+     
    
  #format axis titles
  theme(axis.title = element_text(size = 18))+
  theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 18))+
  xlab(expression(paste(bold("ln["), italic("f"), bold("*"), bold("(1 + "), bold(R[s0]), bold(")/(1 + "), bold(R[s]), bold(")"), bold("]"))))+
  ylab(expression(paste(bold("ln("), bold(R[s]), bold("/"),bold(R[s0]), bold(")"), sep="")))+
   
  #Add plot title
   theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 18, hjust = 0.5))+
   #ggtitle(expression(paste(bold(N^alpha), bold(" and "), bold(N^beta))))+
  
  #format axis lines, text, tick marks
  theme(axis.line = element_line(size=1, colour = "black"))+
  theme(axis.ticks = element_line(color="black", size=1))+
  #theme(axis.ticks.length = unit(0.2, "cm"))+
  
  #format legend
  theme(legend.title = element_blank())+
  theme(legend.text = element_text(size = 16))
  #theme(legend.position = c(0.84,0.3))
  #theme(legend.position = "none")

)


ggsave(plot_N_SP_BW_legend, filename = here("graphs/plot_N_SP_BW_legend.tiff"), height = 3.5, width = 6, units = "in")
```

#Make table with values extracted from the Rayleigh model without approximation where x = ln(f*(1+R_s0)/(1+R_s)) and y = ln(R_s/R_s0) for delta_N, delta_alpha, delta_beta, SP, and delta_18O (N2OR1-3 combined)

  - Make a separate row in the table for each delta type (delta_N, delta_alpha, delta_beta, SP, and delta_18O)
  
  - The linear regression model for the Rayleigh equation for substrate without approximation is defined so that x = ln(f*(1+R_s0)/(1+R_s)) and y = ln(R_s/R_s0)

  - This is Eq. 39 from Hayes, 2004 and Eq. V.17 from Bigeleisen and Wolfsburg, 1958:
ln(R_s/R_s0) = epsilon*ln(f*(1+R_s0)/(1+R_s))

  - slope = epsilon

  - intercept = 0
  
##References
  - Hayes, J.: An Introduction to Isotopic Calculations, Woods Hole Oceanographic Insitution, https://doi.org/10.1575/1912/27058, 2004.
  - Bigeleisen, J. and Wolfsberg, M.: Theoretical and experimental aspects of isotope effects in chemical kinetics, Adv Chem Phys, 1, 15-76, 1958.
```{r N2OR_ray_no_approx, warning=FALSE}
#n = number of loops; in this case, the number of rows in the table
n <- 5

#m = number of models; in this case, m = 1 because we're only using one model (standard Rayleigh)

m <- 1

#Make empty table to store results
N2OR_ray_no_approx <- blank_tb(n, m)

N2OR_ray_no_approx <- mutate(N2OR_ray_no_approx,
  Model = c(
    "BW [Rayleigh w/o approx: x = ln(R_s/R_s0) and y = ln(f*(1+R_s0)/(1+R_s)]"
  ),
  
  Data = c(
    "N2OR Replicates 1-3"
),

  Replicate = "pooled N2OR_1-3",

  Delta_type = c(
    "delta_N",
    "delta_alpha",
    "delta_beta",
    "SP",
    "delta_18O"
  )
) 

for (i in 1:n) {
    data <- IRMS_N2OR_BW
    
  
  if(i == 1){ #First row: delta_N
    y <- IRMS_N2OR_BW$y_N
    x <- IRMS_N2OR_BW$x_N
  } else if(i == 2){ #Second row: delta_alpha
    y <- IRMS_N2OR_BW$y_alpha
    x <- IRMS_N2OR_BW$x_alpha
  } else if(i == 3){ #Third row: delta_beta
    y <- IRMS_N2OR_BW$y_beta
    x <- IRMS_N2OR_BW$x_beta
  } else if(i == 4){ #Fourth row: SP
    y <- IRMS_N2OR_BW$y_SP
    x <- IRMS_N2OR_BW$x_SP        
  } else if (i == 5){ #Fifth row: delta_18O
    y <- IRMS_N2OR_BW$y_18O
    x <- IRMS_N2OR_BW$x_18O    
  }
  

  
  #Apply standard Rayleigh model where x = `-flnf/(1-f)` and y = delta_p, delta_alpha, or delta_beta
    lm_delta <- lm(y ~ x, data = data)
    
    #Fill in table w/ values extracted from standard Rayleigh model
    N2OR_ray_no_approx$Multiple_R_squared[i] = summary(lm_delta)$r.squared
    N2OR_ray_no_approx$RMSE_lm[i] = rmse(model = lm_delta, data = data)
  
    N2OR_ray_no_approx$f_min[i] = min(data$f)
    N2OR_ray_no_approx$f_max[i] = max(data$f)
    
    N2OR_ray_no_approx$delta_s0_meas[i] = initial_deltas$delta_s0_meas[i]
    N2OR_ray_no_approx$se_delta_s0_meas[i] = initial_deltas$se_delta_s0_meas[i]
  
    N2OR_ray_no_approx$delta_s0_calc[i] = "NA"
    N2OR_ray_no_approx$se_delta_s0_calc[i] = "NA"
    
    #To convert dimensionless epsilon to per mil epsilon, multiply by 1000
    N2OR_ray_no_approx$epsilon[i] = as.numeric( lm_delta$coefficients[2])*1000
    
    #To convert dimensionless se_epsilon to per mil se_epsilon, multiply by 1000
    N2OR_ray_no_approx$se_epsilon[i] = summary( lm_delta)$coefficients[2,2]*1000
    
    #ff = 1 + (dimensionless epsilon)
    N2OR_ray_no_approx$ff[i] = 1 +  lm_delta$coefficients[2]
    #se_ff = se_epsilon for dimensionless epsilon
    N2OR_ray_no_approx$se_ff[i] = summary( lm_delta)$coefficients[2,2]    
    
    N2OR_ray_no_approx$KIE[i] = 1/N2OR_ray_no_approx$ff[i]
    N2OR_ray_no_approx$se_KIE[i] = abs(-1/(N2OR_ray_no_approx$ff[i])^2*N2OR_ray_no_approx$se_ff[i])
    
    N2OR_ray_no_approx$pval_epsilon[i] = summary(lm_delta)$coefficients[2,4]
}

write.csv(N2OR_ray_no_approx, here("data/output/N2OR_ray_no_approx.csv"), row.names = TRUE)

(N2OR_ray_no_approx)
```

#Table 2: N2OR_ray_no_approx_summary: Paste mean +/- standard error for values extracted from the Rayleigh model without approximation

When the .csv file is opened in Excel, a funky symbol is included with the +/- symbol, but that can be removed with find and replace.
```{r N2OR_ray_no_approx_summary}

(N2OR_ray_no_approx_summary <- N2OR_ray_no_approx %>% mutate(
  Multiple_R_squared =
    paste(round(as.numeric(N2OR_ray_no_approx$Multiple_R_squared), 2)),
  
  RMSE_lm =
    paste(round(as.numeric(N2OR_ray_no_approx$RMSE_lm), 4) 
  ),
  
  f_min = 
    paste(round(as.numeric(N2OR_ray_no_approx$f_min), 2)
  ),
  
  f_max = 
    paste(round(as.numeric(N2OR_ray_no_approx$f_max), 2)
  ),

  delta_s0_meas = c(
    paste(round(as.numeric(N2OR_ray_no_approx$delta_s0_meas), 1), "\u00B1", round(as.numeric(N2OR_ray_no_approx$se_delta_s0_meas), 1))
  ),
  
  delta_s0_calc = "NA",
   
  epsilon = c(
    paste(round(as.numeric(N2OR_ray_no_approx$epsilon), 1), "\u00B1", round(as.numeric(N2OR_ray_no_approx$se_epsilon), 1))
  ),  

  ff = c(
    paste(round(as.numeric(N2OR_ray_no_approx$ff), 4), "\u00B1", round(as.numeric(N2OR_ray_no_approx$se_ff), 4))
  ),
  
 KIE = c(
    paste(round(as.numeric(N2OR_ray_no_approx$KIE), 4), "\u00B1", round(as.numeric(N2OR_ray_no_approx$se_KIE), 4))
  ),
  
  pval_epsilon = c(
    as.numeric(formatC(N2OR_ray_no_approx$pval_epsilon,  format = "e", digits = 2))
  )

)%>%
    dplyr::select(-se_delta_s0_meas, -se_delta_s0_calc, -se_epsilon, -se_ff, -se_KIE)
)

write.csv(N2OR_ray_no_approx_summary, here("data/output/N2OR_ray_no_approx_summary.csv"), row.names = TRUE)
```

  - N2OR_ray_summary: Mariotti's approximation of the Rayleigh equation; x=lnf, y = delta; all data combined
  - N2OR_ray_no_approx_summary: Rayleigh model without approximation (BW model); x = ln(f*(1+R_s0)/(1+R_s)) and y = ln(R_s/R_s0); all data combined
  
##Note: We cannot directly compare RMSE values between models because the dependent variable (y) is not the same for the no approx (BW) model and Mariotti's approximation of the Rayleigh model.
  
```{r N2OR_all_models_summary}

   N2OR_ray_early_summary,
   N2OR_ray_no_approx_summary
 )
 )
```
